lines.english: "The sun really does set early this time of year, huh…"
"…You're saying that now? The shortest day of the year in Tokyo was almost a month ago."
"Oh, we've got an expert here. In other words, the days are only getting longer and longer from now on… It's still dark though."
"…! Drop the sarcasm, already."
"Huh, I wasn't trying to belittle you or anything. Although, of course, I do think that waking up after 3 PM is unbecoming of a responsible adult."
"Shut up!"
December 31st, New Year's Eve.
Despite being the last commemorative day of the year, we had already lost eight precious hours of it.
Kazusa, who had proudly proclaimed that she would come over in the morning, only woke up once the sun was already well on its way west.
"You sure like getting your own way, don't you?"
"I told you to shut up!"
When I woke up around the usual time, I saw Kazusa and Youko-san peacefully asleep in the living room, firmly in each other's embrace.
Unable to bring myself to break apart such an endearing spectacle,
…I didn't think I'd be forced to order lunch outside as well, though.
"A lot has happened. Take a hint already."
"I told you, I'm not trying to belittle you or anything."
"That's not what your attitude's implying at all."
"That's just… something I was born with."
That's right. I'm not trying to belittle her at all. I'm simply a bit jealous, that's all.
And…
"Hey, Kazusa… never let go of what you have with your mother right now."
I want Youko-san to keep holding on to her life. I want Kazusa to keep loving her mother.
"Huh… That doesn't make any sense."
"Haha… Maybe you're right."
And lastly… um… if they could share with me even the slightest bit of the familial love they have for each other, I'd be really happy.
That's my wish as the newest member of their family.
"Anyway, where are we headed? Aren't we supposed to eat soba, watch the New Year's concert, listen to the temple bells, and then visit the shrine?"
"That's an alluring idea, but there's something I want to show you first."
"But the place you're heading to is…"
"Please."
Because…
There is a place I simply have to visit before the day ends.
"I knew it was this place…"
"Yeah… The place we spent three years in."
Houjou High School.
"I only spent two and a half years here, though."
"You were a delinquent, after all."
"Aah, I just remembered a certain annoying class rep and now I'm pissed off. Let me kick him."
This holy ground that the both of us were thinking of ever since we came back to Japan, but could never bring ourselves to visit until now.
The place we met at…
"But still, it feels different now that no one's here."
"Well, it's New Year's Eve, after all."
The school gates, that lead to both the high school and the nearby university campus, are not closed even on New Year's Eve.
However, the school building is still devoid of life, and paired with the warm colors of the evening sun, the building stands with an air of loneliness.
"Let's go then, Kazusa."
"What, we're going back already?"
"What are you saying? This is our precious alma mater, you know?"
"Ah, hey…"
Kazusa raises her voice in confusion, perhaps not understanding why I'm headed in the direction I am.
"Let's visit, just for a little bit."
"Huh, but… that's trespassing."
"It's fine, I promise. No one's here. How can you call yourself a delinquent if you're gonna get cold feet over this?"
"Wha…! And how can you call yourself a class rep when you're just doing as you please!"
In the end though, either her pride as a delinquent, or her desire to spite the class rep triumphed over her wariness.
Toward the school building.
"Uwa, you had to pick 3-E out of all places…"
"Better than 1-H, isn't it?"
"Shut up."
The entrance leading to the shoe lockers wasn't locked either, so we were able to make it to the school hallways without any obstacle.
…I do think we're being a bit careless, but today is special.
"Still, this place hasn't changed at all either."
Just as Kazusa said earlier, the room plate read 3-E.
"This was my seat, and that one was yours…"
"Yeah, you're right… I can vaguely remember the outside view from here."
And if my memory serves right, this classroom is undoubtedly the same 3-E that we were assigned to.
"Let's see, perhaps some of your old scribbles still remain here. You know, things like music notes, or insults aimed at your teachers…"
"There might be one that says 'Kitahara is a dumbass.'"
"…You wrote that kind of stuff?"
Under the evening sun, in a classroom empty save the two of us, we bring back long forgotten memories to the light.
"Yeah, more times than I can remember. Back then I found you so unbelievably annoying that you definitely were in my top five most hated people."
"Me though… I loved you back then."
"I know that. You're a superficial bastard who falls in love based on how a girl looks, after all."
"That's why back then, I loved looking at you sleeping by the window."
"You sure enjoyed waking me up, though."
"Well obviously. By waking you up I was able to see your face… Could there be a better reward?"
"…Aah, annoying, gross! I can't stand listening to you. You've really turned into an embarrassment, haven't you?"
Although her words are relentless, Kazusa slowly inches toward me until her cheeks touch my chest.
"That's because I live with someone who keeps making me want to say embarrassing things."
"That's gross too. Knock it off."
Normally our conversations end with one of us busting out laughing, making us lose track of whatever we were talking about.
But this time, the quiet, scarlet, cold, dim, and melancholy evening sun preserves our embarrassing memories without letting go.
"This place hasn't changed either."
"No, it hasn't…"
For some reason, Houjou High School has three music rooms.
Music Room 1 is the one that students in the regular program use.
In the school building on the opposite side is Music Room 3, which is reserved for students in the music program.
And lastly there is this place, Music Room 2. A classroom reserved for the best of the music program students, who use it for personal practice.
…At least on paper. Up until a few years back, it was reserved solely for a single delinquent girl.
And this is also our last destination for today…
No… Our last destination in Japan.
"Cold…!"
The moment I open the window, a somewhat powerful gust of wind enters and cools down the whole classroom.
"Obviously. It's New Year's Eve."
"Yeah, it's cold. Even colder than during the school festival."
"Haruki…"
I stick my head out the window and look at the classroom to my right.
It goes without saying that the window to that classroom is tightly shut. No guitar sound can possibly be heard from it.
"Mh, mhmm, cough, cough… H-Hey, Kazusa."
"Look, you're going to catch a cold. Just close the stupid thing already."
"N-No… this isn't a cold."
"Then what is it?"
I'm simply nervous, that's all.
"More importantly… well, um…"
"You're acting strange, you know."
I think I'm acting strangely too.
I've come this far already, but taking the next step is turning into a real struggle.
"S-So, umm… to put it into words…"
"Seriously, what's up with you?"
"I'd like to… listen to you playing the piano."
"…Here?"
"Y-Yeah, right here."
But that's to be expected, I guess.
Everything needs to be done in a certain order for it to work.
As always, she grumbles about how I'm always listening to her play the piano anyway, and that her fingers are too cold to move properly…
And of course, also as always, she relents by saying "This is the last time, okay?" before quietly beginning her performance.
The solitary performance she held every day for three years, using this piano.
The piano that stood by Kazusa for those three years, and which also worsened the friction between her and her classmates.
"Hey, Kazusa."
"Hmm?"
"When did you realize the guitarist was me?"
"It's too far in the past. I can't remember."
The piano that guided my clumsy guitar to greatness. The piano that guided our amateur band to greatness.
And… the piano that after our performance, kept on playing even as Kazusa and I ever so slightly touched, but also went our separate ways.
"Did you match my melody because you knew it was me? Would you have poked your nose in if it was anyone else?"
"I just said I can't remember. It doesn't matter anyway. When it happened doesn't make a difference."
"Doesn't make a difference, huh."
Kazusa still feels regret over the betrayal three years ago.
But there is not a hint of regret over our separation eight years ago anymore.
She has accepted everything, happy and sorrowful, that has brought her to where she is now. All she can do now is smile in recollection.
"Hey, Kazusa."
That's why I'll…
"What is it this time? I'm going out of my way to play for you, and you keep interrupting…"
"Let us start again… right here."
I'll never let go of that smile.
"…Huh?"
On top of the piano… a tiny little box laid before Kazusa's eyes.
"And let us continue together, forever."
And inside it was a gentle, silver glint.
"What… What are you playing at?"
It is the very thing that is still missing from Kazusa's left ring finger.
"I'm sorry… I might have betrayed you just a tiny bit… I conspired with Youko-san."
"Does that mean… Don't tell me…"
"This is the ceremonial hall. This is the day."
"Tomorrow…? In Music Room 2!?"
"That's right. That is the plan for the Kitahara and Touma family banquet."
"At a school, during New Year's… I'm amazed you got permission."
"Well, I have a pretty give-and-take type relationship with Houjou University. Lots of backroom dealings, you see."
"But why…"
"Why, because it's a place that's special to that girl… for better and for worse."
"I didn't mean that… Why on New Year's Eve?"
"That's… well… my own form of revenge, I guess you could say."
"What do you mean?"
"I wanted to retry my old strategy one more time… Just kidding, I'm just being a bit stubborn."
Though up until the very end, Youko-san never really told me what exactly she was referring to when she said she was being stubborn.
"You guys are terrible…!"
Even so, this ceremony, chosen to be held at this place and at this hour, is a product of the exquisite mix of Youko-san's love, tenacity and mischievousness.
"Did you think I'd get overwhelmed by emotions at the sight? Did you expect me to cry?"
"You're not going to cry?"
"Like hell I'd cry, you idiot! I've always said I didn't need a ceremony!"
"You did…?"
The words she spoke when we were snuggling in bed had a slightly different nuance in my memories though.
"And yet you set up this bizarre, forced tearjerker of a surprise… What, did you want to take pictures of me crying just so you can laugh at them later?"
"No, that wasn't my plan…"
"In that case, I refuse to cry even if it kills me! I'll recite my vows in the most boring, monotonous way possible!"
"Fine, you don't have to cry."
If anything, what's amusing is the fact she actually does plan on reciting her vows despite how angry she is.
"Youko-san and I simply did this for our own self-satisfaction. You can just begrudgingly go along with it."
In any case, I've gotten Kazusa's consent.
That's why I take out my phone and press the send button.
"Who are you texting?"
"Why, the family of the bride, of course. As well as her friends."
After all, they're supposed to have been waiting outside for a while.
…And while carrying the bride's ensemble, at that.
"Um, excuse me? Is she still not done?"
"Ah, I'm sorry, Kitahara-san. She actually finished changing a while ago, but…"
"Right…"
Kudou-san, who is in the neighboring Music Room 1, sounded somewhat troubled.
It's been well over an hour since she dragged Kazusa away to change her clothes.
"Um, Kazusa-san has been… grumbling in the hallway for a while…"
"Aah…"
"Get a hold of yourself already, would you? I know you're dying to let him see it."
"T-That's not true! I can't think of anything worse!"
"I'll say it again, why do you have to get so insanely flustered? How old do you think you are? I feel embarrassed to be your mother."
"But, but… Mooom!"
"Oh god, I've had enough! Just go already!"
"S-Stop… Stooop!"
"Ah…"
Well, I did have an idea of what she'd look like…
"You're terrible, all of you…"
I knew that seeing Kazusa dressed like this would blow my socks off.
"I-I-I didn't… I didn't agree to…!"
I knew I'd be at a loss for words.
"…When you heard we were holding a wedding, you knew this would happen, didn't you?"
"B-But, but! Not like… Not like…"
But, how should I put it… I guess even when I'm in a state of complete astoundment, my mouth still moves.
Or rather, since she's even more panicked than I am, I feel an obligation to drive the conversation forward.
"You're beautiful, Kazusa."
"Don't say that!"
To be honest, I want to shout "Holy crap!" at the top of my lungs right now, before embracing Kazusa with all my might.
But Kazusa just looks as though she's really not ready for this.
"B-But… I'm… I'm…"
We've been living together for three years already, and on paper, we're already married.
Yet somehow, the idea of becoming a bride in a wedding ceremony didn't even cross her mind once.
"I only wanted to become your wife. It's not like I ever wanted to be a bride…"
"I don't see the problem. Why not be a bride?"
"B-But, but…!"
Is there still guilt lingering deep down within her?
Up until now, Kazusa never once tried to dress up unless it was for a concert.
Although perhaps that was partially just her personality.
"You're really beautiful… It looks so good on you it's almost ridiculous."
"Haruki…! U-Uaah…!"
"Are you sure you should be crying? Youko-san would gladly record and spread the tape all around."
"Shut up! Shut up! Shut up…!"
"Our bizarre surprise seems to be a huge success…"
From now on, we will never again anguish over what we should have done, and what could have been.
We will never again disavow what we have right now.
That's why we will affirm what we have.
From this place filled with the greatest joys but also the greatest pains, we start again.
With that said, our belated wedding ceremony now commences.
"Hey, Kazusa… I swear to always be by your side."
"I've made that oath a million times already."
"I see…"
"Well, I guess a million times isn't that many… I do."
"Yeah…"
"Hey! Wait a second! You promised you'd say that with me as a witness!"
"…They said they're ready now."
"Then let's go!"
"Yup!"
